prompt:
Repo: /home/user/House-building. Read /home/user/House-building/docs/CONVENTIONS.md first (golden rule: every number on screen is traceable to a named assumption in the file you are about to write). You are read-only in general, but for this job you ARE expected to write exactly one file: /home/user/House-building/docs/research/assumptions.md. Nothing else.

The job: decide and document the construction defaults for a simple residential house-material estimator aimed at Oman / GCC self-builders (a person building their own villa and wanting a rough count of blocks, rebar steel and ready-mix concrete). Choose the construction system yourself — the owner deliberately left it to you — and say why in two lines. The obvious candidate is a reinforced-concrete frame (footings, columns, beams, slabs) with hollow concrete block infill walls, which is how Muscat villas are typically built, but confirm and document it.

Document, with a one-line rationale and a source (URL or named standard/handbook) for each, and a plain "confidence" tag (Certain / Likely / Guessing):
1. Block sizes and counts: standard hollow block dimensions used in Oman (external and internal partition walls), mortar joint thickness, resulting blocks per m² of wall, and a wastage %.
2. Wall geometry rules of thumb: how to derive external wall length and internal wall length from a room list (name, length, width) per floor; typical door/window opening deduction as a %; typical external wall thickness vs internal.
3. Concrete volumes: rules of thumb per m² of built-up area (or per element) for isolated footings + tie beams, columns, beams, slabs (slab thickness), ground slab/plinth — for a 1–4 floor villa. State the grade (e.g. C30/C35) and wastage %.
4. Rebar steel: kg of steel per m³ of concrete per element (footings, columns, beams, slabs) — typical ranges and the single default you pick — plus wastage %.
5. Prices in OMR, as of today (2026-09-22): hollow block per piece (200mm and 150mm), rebar per tonne, ready-mix per m³ (state the grade), and ideally cement bag/sand/aggregate for mortar. Use web search; give the source URL and the date you checked. If a price can't be sourced, say so and give a clearly labelled estimate with confidence "Guessing". These become editable defaults in the UI, never authoritative — say that at the top of the price table.
6. A worked example: a 2-floor, 5-room, ~200 m² per floor villa, with the resulting block count, concrete m³, steel tonnes, and OMR cost, so the builders have a number to test against.

Format the file so a builder can transcribe it straight into a JavaScript DEFAULTS object: give every assumption a short snake_case key (e.g. block_ext_per_m2, rebar_kg_per_m3_columns, price_omr_block_200) in a table with columns: key | value | unit | rationale | source | confidence | last_checked. Keep it under ~200 lines.

Your final message: the file path, the construction system you chose and why (two lines), the six headline numbers of the worked example, and which prices you could not source properly.
report:
File written: docs/research/assumptions.md (115 lines).

Construction system chosen: RC skeleton frame (isolated footings + tie beams, columns, beams, solid slabs) with hollow concrete block infill walls — the standard for Muscat/GCC villas; block-on-frame is faster/cheaper than load-bearing masonry and is what local block factories and contractors design around by default.

Worked example (2-floor, 5-room, ~200 m²/floor = 400 m² villa): ≈5,320 blocks · ≈126 m³ concrete · ≈13.6 tonnes steel · ≈1,330 OMR blocks · ≈4,032 OMR concrete · ≈3,536 OMR steel (≈8,900 OMR materials total).

Prices NOT properly sourced (marked "Guessing"): 200mm and 150mm hollow block unit price, ready-mix C30 per m³, sand, aggregate. Supplier sites (mcp.om, buymaterials.com, alyusroman.com) were blocked by the environment's network proxy; only search snippets were usable. Rebar (≈260 OMR/tonne) and cement (≈1.9 OMR/bag) are sourced but "Likely"/"Guessing".

Orchestrator review: concrete and steel ratios are in the normal villa range. Block count is low because the sample's five rooms cover only half the floor. Amendment appended as section 7: the room list must include every space, and an external-perimeter shape factor was added. Section 6 numbers superseded by the calculator's own sample house.
outcome: assumptions written; orchestrator amended wall rule (section 7)
